entries.title: W&M Faculty Led Study Abroad Program to Bhutan
entries.description: The Royal University of Bhutan (RUB) was founded on June 2, 2003, by royal decree and serves as Bhutan's national university system. During the program, W&M faculty member Dr. Kevin Vose will share the history of Himalayan religions with students. Students will travel throughout the country, gaining perspective regarding the relevance of religious and political buildings, structures, and architecture. Similarly, a local faculty member from the Royal University of Bhutan will illustrate the context, importance and use of the Gross National Happiness Developmental Model. This program is a unique melting pot of history, religious studies, and environmental policy.

entries.title: W&M Faculty Led Study Abroad Program to Cambridge
entries.description:
Cambridge is a city on the River Cam in eastern England, home to the prestigious University of Cambridge, dating back to 1209. There are 31 University Colleges within the University of Cambridge system. University museums have exhibits on archaeology and anthropology, polar exploration, the history of science and zoology and much more.

Program Information: William & Mary’s long-standing summer program in Cambridge, England, is housed in beautiful and historical Christ’s College, one of 31 colleges that comprise the University of Cambridge. Christ’s was founded in 1437 and later endowed by Lady Margaret Beaufort, mother of King Henry VII. Cambridge is about an hour-long train trip from King's Cross Station in central London. Courses for the Summer program generally meet from Mon-Thurs, with excursions on weekends. Possible excursions for this year's program may include day trip(s) to London, and trips to castles and other places of historical and cultural interest. W&M students are housed in comfortable single rooms in Christ's. The program price will include breakfast and partial supplements for other meals.

entries.title: America’s Tapestry: 13 Colonies. 13 Stories. 1 Nation.
entries.description:
Featuring 13 hand-embroidered panels, one for each of the original colonies, America’s Tapestry illustrates the diverse stories of individual contributions — many overlooked — that reveal each colony’s struggle for independence. Collaboratively stitched by artisans from New Hampshire to Georgia, the panels weave together stories from our nation’s founding through the medium of embroidery to commemorate our country’s 250th anniversary. The project was developed and curated by Stefan Romero.

The Virginia panel was stitched at the Muscarelle by members of the Williamsburg Rose and Thistle Chapter of the Embroidery Guild of America, along with community volunteers, under the direction of Catherine Theron. This exhibition, in collaboration with William & Mary’s Office of Strategic Cultural Partnerships, is supported by a grant from the Coby Foundation during The Year of Civic Leadership at William & Mary and the nationwide America250 celebration.

entries.title: Student Employment Fall Hiring Office Hours (Session #2)
entries.description:
Join the Student Employment Fall Hiring Office Hours Teams Meeting

The Financial Aid Office's Student Employment team invites departmental supervisors, hiring managers, and administrative staff to attend our Student Employment Office Hours. These informal sessions provide an opportunity to:

  • Receive important student employment updates and reminders
  • Learn about upcoming deadlines and process changes
  • Ask questions about hiring student employees in Workday
  • Troubleshoot hiring and employment-related issues
  • Discuss Federal Work-Study policies and procedures

Whether you're new to student employment or have specific questions about a current hire, stop by and join the conversation. No formal agenda is required, and attendees are welcome to join for the full session or just a portion of the time. Topics may include:

  • Student hiring procedures
  • Student employment policies and compliance
  • Supervisor and student responsibilities
  • Form I-9s
  • Workday hiring tasks
  • Employment verification policy
  • Federal Work-Study management

Your participation will not only help improve your department's student hiring workflow but also help us identify common challenges and improve student employment processes for departments across campus. Bring your questions, and we'll be happy to help!

entries.title: Special Collections Community Open House
entries.description: Explore the stories behind rare books, letters, diaries, photographs, maps, and other remarkable items from the Special Collections Research Center in the Earl Gregg Swem Library at William & Mary for an open house of treasures at the James City County Library, 7770 Croaker Road. Drop in between 11am-2pm to view selected materials up close, learn how they illuminate local and regional history, and talk with staff about how these unique collections are preserved and used for research. Highlights include the Frenchman’s Maps of Williamsburg from 1782, a hand drawn map of Jamestown Island during the Civil War, a first edition of the Book of Mormon, letters and documents from our Founding Fathers and Mothers, a 1700’s James City Legal Form book, and letters by the Marquis de Lafayette during the American Revolution. This welcoming event is open to anyone curious about the past and the fascinating objects that help bring it to life.

entries.title: After Hours Lecture Series: Talkin' Terrapins
entries.description:
Join us for our August After Hours lecture, where Dr. Chambers will discuss some of the challenges to the conservation of diamondback terrapins in Virginia coastal waters. Diamondback terrapins can live for decades, provided the multiple habitats they use are connected and available. Sometimes, however, resource use by humans conflicts with resources required by turtles. What are the issues that most threaten terrapin populations, and what can we do to promote the conservation of North America’s only fully estuarine turtle? Dr. Chambers will present his tale of the terrapin, with a focus on efforts to protect terrapins from drowning as bycatch in Virginia’s blue crab fishery.

Registration is required.

We are excited to offer this lecture in-person in Davis Hall on our Gloucester Point Campus! This lecture will also be available as a live-streamed webinar. Registration is required for both in-person and webinar attendees. Webinar links will be sent in all registration confirmation emails. This event will be photographed and/or videotaped. By attending this event, each participant consents to being photographed and/or videotaped and authorizes the Batten School & VIMS to use such photographs and videos for media purposes.

entries.title: W&M Lifelong Learning: AI for All Session 3
entries.description:
Join Doug Schmidt, Dean of the School of Computing, Data Sciences & Physics, and Dan Runfola, Chair of the Data Science Department, for the next installment of the AI for All series, where we will explore the rapidly evolving world of agentic AI. Whether you are new to AI or looking to deepen your understanding, this interactive session moves beyond basic prompting to demonstrate how AI systems can plan, reason, coordinate multiple tools, and accomplish complex, multi-step tasks through agentic orchestration frameworks.

Through live demonstrations and guided examples, participants will see how modern AI agents can combine large language models with external tools, data sources, and workflows to automate sophisticated tasks, support decision-making, accelerate research, and enhance productivity. We'll examine practical orchestration frameworks, illustrate real-world use cases, and discuss emerging best practices for designing reliable, human-centered AI systems. By the end of the session, participants will have a clearer understanding of how agentic AI differs from traditional chat-based interactions and how these powerful capabilities can be applied in both professional and personal settings.

This virtual event is free and open to the public and is part of the William & Mary Alumni Association’s Lifelong Learning program.

entries.title: Opening Convocation
entries.description:
Typically on the first day of classes, faculty, staff and students gather at the Sir Christopher Wren Building to signify the beginning of the academic year and to officially welcome all of our entering William & Mary students. At the conclusion of the ceremony each year, the official party leads those in attendance around the building to the opposite side. According to our tradition, all students who are new to W&M remain at the ceremony site with the university President. Then, at the tolling of the Wren Building bell, the President leads the group in a special procession through the portico of the building to the other side, where the new students are warmly welcomed by current members of the faculty, staff and student body. A festive campus-wide celebration follows for the entire campus community.

Not unlike the Commencement exercises which mark the close of an academic session, this ceremony is a time of affirming and enhancing the sense of community which exists at William & Mary. It is a time of achieving focus, of highlighting themes we know to be important to our current condition, and of reaffirming those things we value and share. We welcome you to join us each fall as we honor our newest William & Mary students!

entries.title: Bray School Stories: Records and Research with Virginia Untold: The African American Narrative
entries.description: Join W&M Bray School Lab genealogist, Elizabeth Drembus, as she turns a spotlight on the records and the work of the Library of Virginia, specifically the library’s ongoing project “Virginia Untold: The African American Narrative.” Elizabeth welcomes Lydia Neuroth, Project Manager of “Virginia Untold” and Elle Kim, Part-time Project Archivist (and former Bray School Lab intern) as they discuss this incredible project and share their ongoing work to digitize records that document some of the lived experiences of enslaved and free Black and multiracial people in the Library of Virginia’s collections. These records are an incredibly valuable source of information for family historians and have provided important evidence for the Bray School Lab’s genealogical research of the students who attended the Williamsburg Bray School. Please join us! All are welcome!

entries.title: PDF Remediation for Accessibility
entries.description: Do you have complex PDFs that need remediation? Are you new to Adobe Acrobat or looking for a more technical understanding of PDF accessibility? Join our virtual hands-on PDF Accessibility Remediation Training to learn how to identify and fix common accessibility issues in PDF documents. Using a sample PDF, we'll walk through the remediation process step by step, including how to interpret Adobe Acrobat's Accessibility Checker results, address common errors, improve document structure, and ensure content is accessible to all users. This session is ideal for anyone who creates, manages, or remediates PDFs and wants to build practical skills in accessible document design. Time will be reserved for questions and discussion throughout the training. Registration required.

entries.title: Remote Area Medical Interest Meeting
entries.description:
Join us for our first RAM meeting of the 26-27 academic year, on 9/2 at 8pm in ISC 2280‼️

What is RAM?

RAM is a national nonprofit dedicated to providing free medical, dental, and vision care to people all across the US, with no ID or insurance required.

What does our William & Mary chapter do?

As a chapter, we travel to RAM clinics up and down the East Coast, volunteering at RAM clinics to make glasses, clean dental equipment, register patients, and assist providers. We also volunteer with local organizations (such as Williamsburg House of Mercy, Olde Towne Medical and Dental Center, and the Williamsburg Lions Club) to get William & Mary students more involved in our community!

When and where does RAM meet?

We meet monthly on Wednesdays in ISC 2280.

Who can join RAM? ‍♀️

Anyone can join our RAM chapter! Most of our members are pre-med, pre-pa/nursing, or pre-dental students, but we welcome students of all years, majors, and pathways!

RAM is a national nonprofit dedicated to providing free medical, dental, and vision care to people all across the US, with no ID or insurance required.

As a chapter, we travel to RAM clinics up and down the East Coast, volunteering at RAM clinics to make glasses, clean dental equipment, register patients, and assist providers. We meet monthly on Wednesdays in ISC 2280.

entries.description:
REVIVE! Lay Rescuer Training is a hands-on, empowering workshop that teaches you how to respond confidently in an opioid overdose emergency. This training is Virginia’s official Opioid Overdose and Naloxone Education Program, designed for everyday people — no medical background needed. You’ll learn how to recognize the signs of an overdose and safely administer Narcan® (Naloxone) nasal spray to potentially save someone’s life. Why should you come?

  • Learn life-saving skills in an hour
  • Get certified & walk away with a free Naloxone Kit
  • Be part of a movement that’s changing lives & giving second chances

This training is for all members of the W&M Community, whether you're a student leader, a future healthcare professional, or just someone who wants to be prepared.

entries.title: Discovery Lab: Exploring the Deep!
entries.description:
Dive into the mysterious world of the deep sea at this exciting, family-friendly Discovery Lab event! Discover incredible creatures that glow in the dark, survive crushing pressures, and thrive in one of Earth's least-explored environments through hands-on, interactive activities and demonstrations. Explore the technology used to study the ocean's depths, and uncover the secrets hidden miles beneath the surface. Dr. Jenny Dreyer, a marine invertebrate zoologist and curator of the Batten School & VIMS' Invertebrate Collection, will provide an engaging presentation on her past research on deep sea habitats and organisms. Perfect for curious minds of all ages, this event offers a fun and unforgettable adventure into the ocean's final frontier.

Discovery Labs are free, family-friendly programs provided each month by educators at the Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve in Virginia (CBNERR-VA) and the Batten School & VIMS. Designed with elementary-aged youth and their parents in mind, each lab focuses on a different topic related to the Chesapeake Bay and our local environment and includes exhibits, demonstrations, and hands-on activities as well as a short presentation (from 6:30-7:00 PM) by an expert on the topic.

Reservations to this event are required due to limited space.
